piece.headline: HAALAND BLANKS AGAIN, ARORA STAYS CLEAR
piece.standfirst: Haaland let the armbands down for a second week running, and Kartik's N.Jackson punt took the week while the top 3 barely budged.
piece.big_picture: 76 managers backed Haaland. He blanked for the second week running, and the faith is starting to look like a habit. Rajat Arora still stretched his lead to 18 over Neol. Arora keeps winning the title race on other people's mistakes.
piece.decision_of_the_week: Swapnil picked the wrong 11 and left 26 points on the bench. That is more than a whole decent week for some managers. Great squad, wrong lineup. The sort of week that makes you check the team sheet twice.
piece.one_to_watch: Prathap holds the last big-prize place and Cherag sits just 2 behind. Cherag is a 2-time champion and has been in that zone before. If Prathap's run of good weeks stalls, the place could flip.

winners.name: Kartik
winners.verdict: Put the armband on N.Jackson and got 22 back. Season best from a manager who had been crawling up the table. Nerve and skill.

winners.name: Sahil
winners.verdict: Sahil brought in Vuskovic and the week flipped. From 42nd to 19th, the best jump of the lot. Sharp move, sharper timing.

winners.name: Sidharth
winners.verdict: Third week running above average. Gabriel on the armband did the lifting. Not a fluke any more: this is a climb.

losers.name: Janit
losers.verdict: 5th week running below average. A tough run, and the table is being unkind. One good gameweek would change the mood.

losers.name: Vivek
losers.verdict: Worst week of the season for Vivek. The slide to 92nd is 4 weeks old now. Somebody check the team news.

losers.name: Hardik
losers.verdict: Worst week of the season, and Free Fall was the right award. Hardik dropped 23 places in one go. Ouch.
